copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Argentina v Algeria in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Wednesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Argentina side by +12.4pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

On Elo, Argentina comes in 390 points ahead — Argentina at 2140, Algeria at 1750. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Argentina to win at 81%, the draw at 10%, and Algeria to win at 9%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Argentina to win at 69%, the draw at 20%, and Algeria to win at 10%. On the Argentina side specifically the market reads 69%, which prices out at American odds of −223. Compared against the model's 81%, that's the +12.4pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Argentina the lower bound is 77%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +8.0pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 26 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Argentina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.4pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Argentina will hope to defend their title from 2022 after following it up with the Copa América in 2024.

copy.summary: Argentina are favourites on the market at 69% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 81%, a +12.4pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
copy.title: Argentina v Algeria · the model leans Argentina
